title: BGP Attributes: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: B G P often has several ways to reach the same place. It picks one using tags on each route. Those tags are called path attributes.

scenes.heading: Airline baggage tags
scenes.narration: Every bag carries tags that decide its route. A S path lists the networks the route passed through, and shorter wins. Local preference sets which exit your own network prefers. M E D hints to a neighbour which entrance you prefer. Prepending adds extra A S numbers to make a route look worse.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. M E D influences inbound traffic. Prepending makes a route less attractive. By default, M E D is only compared for the same neighbouring A S.

items.right: Only from the same neighbouring AS

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva BGP attributes lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Shorter A S path wins. Local preference is outbound, and M E D is inbound. Prepending makes a route less attractive. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva BGP attributes lab.
